blocks.text: I can define function notation.
Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A function is a mathematical relationship that uniquely maps values of one set to the values of another set.
The domain of a function is the set of values that the mapping is performed on.
The range of a function is the set of values mapped to by the function and the stated domain.

blocks.text: A function like ×3 + 5 uniquely maps an input to an output. All of the inputs make up the domain, and all of the possible outputs make up the range.
If we perform this function on x, we get 3x + 5. This is called “the function 3x + 5”, but we write it using shorthand notation.
The notation means the whole function does not need to be written out each time. It should always be defined at the start.

pairs.a: x is multiplied by 6 and then 2 is added
x is multiplied by 2 and then 6 is added
x is squared and then 6 is added

blocks.text: Andeep asks: “In algebra, ab means a × b. Doesn’t that mean f(x) is the same as f × x?”

blocks.label: Sam’s answer
blocks.text: In algebra ab is a × b, but f(x) is function notation. f(x) means “a function of x”. In f(x), x is still a variable, but the f is not a variable.

options: f(x) means f multiplied by x
f(x) means a function of x
blocks.why: f(x) means “a function of x”. It does not mean f × x.

blocks.text: Graphing f(x) = 3x + 5 uses the same skills as graphing the equation y = 3x + 5. The x values go into the function and the outputs are plotted.
You might see the vertical axis labelled f(x), or you might see it labelled y. When that happens you will see y = f(x).

We can name other functions too: g(x), h(x) and so on. This is useful when several functions are graphed on the same axes, such as f(x) = 3x + 5 and g(x) = 7 − 2x. We write y = g(x) for the second graph.
A valid function uniquely maps all inputs onto a value in the range. The relationship f(x) = 1/x is not a valid function, because 0 is not a valid input.
We make it valid by restricting the domain: f(x) = 1/x, x ≠ 0. Now every value in the domain can be uniquely mapped onto a value in the range.

blocks.q: Which domain restriction is needed for f(x) = 3/(x − 4)?
blocks.why: When x = 4 the denominator is 0, and we cannot divide by 0.

Sam is mapping the function f(x) = 10 − 4x. Sam says: “I know that f(2) = 2, so I think f(−2) = −2. It must be the opposite.”

blocks.label: Show Sam why this is wrong
blocks.text: Evaluate it: f(−2) = 10 − 4(−2) = 10 + 8 = 18. It is always a good idea to test your thinking.

pairs.b: Evaluate the function for the given value of x, then multiply the result by 2
Multiply the given value of x by 4, then substitute this value into the function

blocks.text: f(x) = 3x − 10. Evaluate each of these when x = 8.
It is important to multiply x by 4 {before} performing the function on it.

blocks.q: g(x) = 5x + 2. Evaluate each of these when x = 4.

blocks.text: f(x) = 2x + 7 and g(x) = 3x + 2. Evaluate f(4) + g(5).
Andeep wants to simplify first: f(x) + g(x) = 5x + 9. Sam spots a problem: what x value would we substitute in, 4 or 5?
We cannot combine the functions here, because there are two different x values. Evaluate f(4) and g(5) {separately}, then add.

blocks.q: f(x) = 3x + 1 and g(x) = 10 − 2x. What is f(2) + g(4)?

items: f(x) means “a function of x” and not f × x.
An efficient way to write “x is multiplied by 7 then add 3” is f(x) = 7x + 3.
Multiple functions can be written like this: f(x), g(x), h(x) and so on.
Functions can be manipulated and evaluated, for example f(2), g(5), h(−1) and 6f(2).

flashcards.back:
“A function of x”. It does not mean f × x.

In f(x), x is still a variable, but the f is not a variable.

flashcards.front: Why do we use function notation?
flashcards.back: It is a shorthand: the whole function does not need to be written out each time. It should always be defined at the start.

flashcards.front: How can the vertical axis be labelled when we graph a function?
flashcards.back: f(x), or y. When it is y you will see y = f(x).

flashcards.front: How can we name more than one function?
flashcards.back: f(x), g(x), h(x) and so on.

flashcards.front: Why is f(x) = 1/x not a valid function, and how do we fix it?
flashcards.back:
0 is not a valid input.

Restrict the domain: f(x) = 1/x, x ≠ 0.
Evaluate the function for the given value of x, then multiply the result by 2.
Multiply the given value of x by 4, then substitute this value into the function.
Add 5 to the given value of x, then substitute this value into the function.

flashcards.front: f(x) = 2x + 7 and g(x) = 3x + 2. How do you evaluate f(4) + g(5)?
flashcards.back:
Evaluate f(4) and g(5) separately, then add: 15 + 17 = 32.

We cannot combine the functions first, because the x values are different.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Defining function notation
worksheet.instructions: Work out each value. Answer with a number.

questions.prompt: h(x) = x³ − x². What is h(−2)?
Sam is mapping f(x) = 15 − 7x. Sam knows f(2) = 1 and thinks f(−2) = −1. What is the true value of f(−2)?
questions.explanation: f(−2) = 15 − 7(−2) = 15 + 14 = 29, so it is not the opposite.

questions.prompt: f(x) = 7x + 12 and g(x) = 8 − 7x. Evaluate f(1) + g(2).

f(x) = 3x + 9 and g(x) = 8 − x. Evaluate f(3) + g(4).
questions.explanation: f(3) = 18 and g(4) = 4. The x values are different, so evaluate separately: 18 + 4 = 22.
